fields.Back: An NLP algorithmic trader project that analyzes comment sentiment to inform trading decisions.

fields.Front: What language was the BUFFET data-ingestion pipeline built in?
How many comments did the BUFFET pipeline ingest?
What uptime did the BUFFET ingestion pipeline achieve?
What sentiment analysis model did BUFFET build on?
fields.Back: VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner).

fields.Front: Why use VADER as the base sentiment model instead of training a sentiment classifier from scratch?
fields.Back: VADER is a lightweight, rule-based lexicon model tuned for short, informal text and needs no training data or model training — it can be used and extended out of the box, ideal for fast iteration on high-volume comment sentiment.

fields.Front: How did you improve VADER's accuracy for BUFFET?
fields.Back: By enhancing it with a custom financial lexicon.

fields.Front: What accuracy gain did the custom financial lexicon provide?
What does injecting a custom financial lexicon into VADER actually do?
fields.Back: It adds finance-specific terms and their sentiment valence scores — words/phrases missing from VADER's general-purpose lexicon — so the model correctly scores financial sentiment that generic VADER would misread or ignore.

fields.Front: Why does generic VADER underperform on financial/trading comments without customization?
fields.Back: VADER's default lexicon is tuned for general social-media language and doesn't capture domain-specific financial slang and terms, so it misjudges sentiment specific to trading discussion.

fields.Front: What operational challenge did the BUFFET Python pipeline have to manage?
fields.Back: API rate limits from the data source(s) it ingested comments from.

fields.Front: How did the pipeline maintain 99.9% uptime while respecting API rate limits?
fields.Back: It was engineered to actively manage and throttle requests against the API's rate limits, avoiding being blocked or dropped while continuously ingesting comment data.

fields.Front: What is the end goal of BUFFET's sentiment pipeline?
fields.Back: To feed sentiment signals from ingested comments into algorithmic trading decisions.

fields.Front: What kind of data source likely produced the 63,000+ comments for BUFFET?
fields.Back: A social/community platform with public trading discussion, accessed via a rate-limited API.

fields.Front: STAR — Talking point: Describe the BUFFET reliability challenge and how you solved it.
fields.Back: Task: continuously ingest a high volume of comments (63,000+) through a rate-limited API without downtime. Action: built a Python pipeline that actively managed API rate limits. Result: sustained 99.9% uptime on ingestion.

fields.Front: STAR — Talking point: How did you improve sentiment accuracy for financial text specifically?
fields.Back: Task: generic VADER sentiment scoring didn't capture financial/trading slang. Action: built and injected a custom financial lexicon into VADER. Result: +18% accuracy improvement in sentiment classification for the trading use case.

fields.Front: STAR — Talking point: Why was VADER the right starting point rather than a deep-learning sentiment model?
fields.Back: Task: needed fast, interpretable sentiment scoring on large volumes of short comments. Action: chose rule-based VADER and extended it with a domain-specific financial lexicon rather than training a heavier model from scratch. Result: a meaningful (+18%) accuracy gain with a lightweight, explainable, easily-tunable approach.

fields.Front: STAR — Talking point: Summarize BUFFET's technical contribution in one breath.
fields.Back: A Python pipeline that reliably ingested 63,000+ comments at 99.9% uptime under API rate limits, and boosted VADER sentiment accuracy 18% with a custom financial lexicon — powering an NLP algorithmic trading signal.
A lexicon/rule-based sentiment analysis tool; in BUFFET it was enhanced with a custom financial lexicon for a +18% accuracy gain.
